title: The Trinity
description:
Experience the legendary collaboration between G.H. Hardy and J.E. Littlewood, and their
                        discovery of the self-taught genius Srinivasa Ramanujan. This group represents one of the most
                        productive and poetic eras in Cambridge mathematics.

title: The Bernoulli Dynasty
description:
The Bernoullis were a family of Swiss mathematicians whose brilliance was matched only by their
                        fierce internal rivalries. From the foundations of calculus to the principles of fluid dynamics,
                        they redefined what a scientific family could achieve.

title: The Great Rivalries
description:
Behind the most profound discoveries in science and mathematics lay fierce intellectual battles.
                        From the dispute over the invention of calculus to the nature of gravity, discover the
                        intense rivalries between these giants of the 17th century.

title: Foundations of Computing
description:
Long before the first silicon chip, these visionaries laid the intellectual groundwork for the
                        modern computer. From mechanical engines to Boolean logic, information theory, and game theory,
                        discover how the digital age was born across two centuries.

title: Probability Begins
description:
From gambling problems to classical probability theory. These thinkers transformed our
                        understanding of chance, risk, and uncertainty, moving mathematics from deterministic proofs to
                        statistical models.

title: French Analysis Trio
description:
PDEs, heat, orthogonal functions, and applied analysis. During a golden age of French
                        mathematics, these three redefined how we use math to describe the physical world.

title: Women in Early Mathematics
description:
Breaking through the barriers of their time, these women made fundamental contributions to
                        theoretical and applied mathematics, inspiring generations of mathematicians to follow.

title: The Italian Cubic Wars
description:
One of the most dramatic episodes in mathematical history. Stolen proofs, public debates,
                        and accusations of poisoning surrounded the race to solve the cubic equation in 16th-century
                        Italy. Listen to these four stories together to follow the full, scandalous saga.

title: The Abel–Galois Generation
description:
Two of the greatest mathematical minds of the 19th century, both dead before 30. Abel and
                        Galois independently revolutionized algebra and group theory while struggling for recognition.
                        Liouville was the man who finally brought Galois's work to the world.

title: The Göttingen School
description:
From roughly 1870 to 1933, the University of Göttingen was the world center of mathematics.
                        These four figures shaped modern abstract mathematics — from the 23 Hilbert problems
                        to the birth of abstract algebra — before the school was tragically dismantled by the Nazis.

title: The Electromagnetic Theorists
description:
Maxwell unified electricity and magnetism with mathematics — and then these three took that
                        torch and ran with it. Kelvin, Heaviside, and Hertz each extended and experimentally confirmed
                        electromagnetic theory, reshaping how we understand waves, fields, and energy.

title: Game Theory & Information Age
The Precalculus Pioneers
description:
Centuries before Newton and Leibniz, mathematicians across the Islamic world, South Asia,
                        and Europe were quietly building the foundations that calculus would rest upon — infinite
                        series, trigonometry, positional arithmetic, and algebraic notation.
